newsitem.title: FRANCE: More than 300 targeted in French paedophile probe.
newsitem.headline: More than 300 targeted in French paedophile probe.

text.p: The number of people targeted by French investigations of paedophile videos has risen to more than 300 after high-profile raids that have triggered four suicides, police sources said on Sunday.

A total of 323 people have been placed under investigation by magistrates after unprecedented police swoops on hundreds of homes in France since Tuesday, most of them suspected clients of a firm selling videos featuring sexual abuse of minors.
The figure was up from 210 before the weekend.
Four men, questioned by police over links to child sex offences in recent days, have committed suicide, raising questions about whether France has gone too far in the public shaming of suspects.

In the latest suicide, a 39-year-old teacher, suspected by prosecutors of taking pornographic photographs of minors but not directly linked to the video network, leapt to his death from a bridge in the southern city of Bordeaux on Saturday.

TF1 television on Sunday quoted the prosecutor leading the hunt into the sex videos, Jean-Louis Coste, as calling the suicides regrettable. But it said he also asked who the police were really meant to be protecting in France.
No one has yet been tried. Being placed under investigation in France is short of an indictment but is often a first step towards a trial.
Some 2,500 police were involved in the raids, which have ensnared teachers and clergymen on the mailing list of a company in the central city of Macon.

Police believe the suspected ringleader, Bernard Alapetite, copied foreign child sex videos -- featuring rapes of boys aged under 15 and even sex with animals -- and sold them for 800 francs ($140) each.
